examples: Despite its name, Barry Island is actually a peninsula.

senses.definition: An entity surrounded by other entities that are very different from itself.
examples: The quiet library was an island of tranquility in the noisy, bustling city.
An island of colors on a butterfly's wing.

senses.definition: A superstructure on an aircraft carrier's deck.
Placed or standing apart or alone; in isolation.
examples: An isolated tree in the mountains.

senses.definition: Happening or occurring only once.
examples: Isolated case.
An isolated occurrence.

senses.definition: Such that no pawn of the same color is in an adjacent file.
Affecting ten to twenty percent of a forecast zone.
The state of being isolated, detached, or separated; the state of being away from other people.
examples: She lived her final year in complete isolation, not wanting to see anybody.

senses.definition: The act of isolating.
The state of not having diplomatic relations with other countries (either with most or all other countries, or with specified other countries).
The obtaining of an element from one of its compounds, or of a compound from a mixture.
An important subject or problem that people are discussing or arguing about.
examples: Housing was the main issue at the debate.
Let us deal with the safety issues first.
Money is not the issue here; time is.

senses.definition: To officially give out or announce something.
examples: The embassy issued a warning to travellers.
Each employee is issued with a security pass.

senses.definition: The third-person singular neuter personal pronoun used to refer to an inanimate object, abstract entity, or non-human living thing.
examples: Take this book and put it on the shelf.
Take each day as it comes.
I found a poor little cat. It seems to be half starving.

senses.definition: A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to a baby or child, especially of unknown gender.
examples: She took the baby and held it in her arms.

senses.definition: Refers to someone being identified, often on the phone, but not limited to this situation.
examples: It's me, John.
Somebody wanted a drink, didn't they? Who was it?
It is I, your king.

senses.definition: The impersonal pronoun, used without referent as the subject of an impersonal verb or statement (known as the dummy pronoun, dummy it or weather it).
examples: It is nearly 10 o’clock.
It’s very cold today.

senses.definition: A distinct physical object.
examples: Tweezers are great for manipulating small items.

senses.definition: An object that can be picked up for later use.
A line of text having a legal or other meaning; a separate particular in an account.
examples: The items in a bill.
In response to the first item, we deny all wrongdoing.

senses.definition: A question on a test, which may include its answers.
examples: The exam has 100 items, each of which includes a correct response and three distractors.

senses.definition: Belonging to it.
The one (or ones) belonging to it.
examples: … both Houses have resolved to rob the North of a good friend of its and yours.

senses.definition: It; A thing as the object of a verb or preposition that also appears as the subject.
examples: When the opportunity presented itself, no feasible course of action suggested itself (to us).

senses.definition: It; used to intensify the subject, especially to emphasize that it is the only participant in the predicate.
examples: The door itself is quite heavy.
